simple.meaning: שָׂטָה (sâṭâh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to deviate from duty.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 6 times across Numbers, Proverbs, beginning at Numbers 5:12. Its contexts include faith, Torah, priesthood, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שָׂטָה (H7847).

timeline.evidenceText: “Speak to the children of Israel, and tell them: ‘If any man’s wife goes astray and is unfaithful to him,

The priest shall cause her to take an oath and shall tell the woman, “If no man has lain with you, and if you haven’t gone aside to uncleanness, being under your husband’s authority, be free from this water of bitterness that brings a curse.
But if you have gone astray, being under your husband’s authority, and if you are defiled, and some man has lain with you besides your husband—”
“ ‘This is the law of jealousy, when a wife, being under her husband, goes astray, and is defiled,
Avoid it, and don’t pass by it.
Don’t let your heart turn to her ways.

definitions.full: H7847. satah [ שָׂטָה ] verb turn aside (Aramaic סְטָא , id. ; שְׂטָא stray ; Ethiopic III. be seduced , etc.; cf Dr JPhil. xi (1882), 205 ); — Qal Perfect 2feminine singular שָׂטִית Num 5:19-20 , Imperfect 3feminine singular תִּשְׂטֶה 5:12 ; 5:29 , jussive 3masculine singular יֵשְׂטְ Prov 7:25 ; Imperative masculine singular שְׂטֵה 4:15 ; — turn aside , of unfaithful wife Num 5:12 (absolute), + אִישׁ תַּחַת , i.e. while married, 5:19 (+ טֻמְאָה adverb accusative), 5:20 ; 5:29 (all P); of youth, from ( מֵעַל ) way of evil woman Prov 4:15 , toward ( אֶל ) her ways 7:25 .
